🇸🇦🇸🇾 Saudi Arabia asked Syria to provide manpower to fight Ansar Allah, but Damascus refused, Türkiye Today reports, citing its sources.

The Syrian government "politely" declined a request to organize and deploy Syrian forces against Ansar Allah. One source said the matter is closed: the request was made several months ago, and Syria refused, saying it is focused on its own military organization process and does not intend to enter the conflict as a third party.

Earlier, West Asian outlets claimed that Turkey had sent to Yemen militants under its control from the former "Syrian National Army", now integrated into the Syrian armed forces. Türkiye Today denies this. Regional sources familiar with events in Yemen also refuted reports of an organized deployment, saying no Turkish program to transfer Syrians to Yemen exists.

Interestingly, Syria has close ties with the UAE. In May 2025, the UAE Foreign Ministry welcomed Trump's decision to lift sanctions, calling it a significant step to support Syria's development and prosperity. In July 2026, the UAE welcomed the start of the process of removing Syria from the list of state sponsors of terrorism, and Washington completed the removal in August. In May, Damascus hosted the first Syrian-Emirati investment forum, attended by President al-Sharaa, where the sides reached preliminary agreements on dozens of investment projects.

Given how zealously the Emirates are now working to bring about Saudi failures in Yemen, it cannot be ruled out that Abu Dhabi strongly advised Damascus to refuse the House of Saud.
